claims.text: The target materials are high-melting refractory materials.
Developing a more efficient potential can reduce the computational cost of calculating melting properties.
Reparameterizing an existing potential can reduce the computational cost of calculating melting properties.
The proposed potential development or reparameterization can preserve calculation accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The relevant computational framework is density functional theory.
The baseline ab initio free-energy approach uses thermodynamic integration based on ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Thermodynamic integration in the baseline approach is computationally expensive.
Improving the efficiency of thermodynamic integration reduces computational cost.
The proposed approach can accurately calculate melting temperature.
The proposed approach can accurately calculate entropy of fusion.
The proposed approach can accurately calculate enthalpy of fusion.
The proposed approach can accurately calculate volume change at the melting point.
The proposed approach will reduce computational cost relative to the existing ab initio free-energy approach.
Whether the proposed potential can maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost is uncertain and requires testing.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome state that accuracy will be preserved, whereas the uncertainty field says that maintaining accuracy is uncertain and requires testing.
